target: A CI intake service receives jobs as a Poisson process at 4 jobs per minute. Each identical worker has exponential service time with mean 40 seconds (rate 1.5 jobs per minute). Jobs wait in one shared FIFO queue. The SLO requires mean queueing delay, before service, no more than 30 seconds. The team must choose the smallest stable integer worker count supported by this queueing model.
surface: A previous CI service chose three workers because aggregate capacity, 3*1.5=4.5 jobs per minute, exceeded the 4-job-per-minute average arrival rate. It used utilization below 100% as the only staffing gate.
structural: A call center modeled Poisson arrivals, exponential handling, c parallel agents, and one FIFO queue as M/M/c. It used Erlang C: a=lambda/mu, rho=a/c; P(wait)=[a^c/(c!*(1-rho))]/[sum(k=0 to c-1) a^k/k! + a^c/(c!*(1-rho))]; mean queue wait Wq=P(wait)/(c*mu-lambda). It evaluated adjacent stable integers and chose the smallest whose Wq met the wait SLO.
rubric: Explicitly selects an M/M/c Erlang-C queueing calculation, not utilization alone.
Uses lambda=4/minute, mu=1.5/minute, and evaluates c=3 versus c=4.
Finds Wq for c=3 is about 1.60 minutes and for c=4 about 0.189 minutes (11.4 seconds).
Chooses four workers as the smallest count meeting the 30-second queue-wait SLO.
Notes reliance on Poisson arrivals, exponential service, a shared FIFO queue, and steady-state stability.
